html:
SMTO-SKL-0051 — SMTO couldn't carry out this Google Drive request as asked

GUID: 57c010c2-cf5d-5430-ad64-80e87fe10cbb
Slug: google-drive-invalid-arguments
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-drive

What happened

  • SMTO stopped because the details of your Google Drive request didn't fit together, such as a missing file, a destination that isn't a usable folder, or an unclear move. Nothing in your Drive was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to find the file first (for example "show me the file called Budget 2026 in my Drive"), then ask for the change on that exact file. A change needs the file's exact identity and its latest version, which SMTO gets by looking the file up first.
  2. If you are saving into or moving to a folder, name a folder that exists and isn't in the Drive trash. For a move, say which folder the file should leave. SMTO refuses a destination that isn't a folder, is in the trash, or would leave the file in more than one place.
  3. If the file is a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file, ask SMTO to upload your file as a new copy instead of replacing the existing one. SMTO can't overwrite the contents of Google's own document types with an uploaded file.
  4. Before asking again for a change such as a move or rename, open Google Drive and check the file is still as you expect. If someone else changed the file meanwhile, checking first avoids repeating or undoing their work.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the file, folder or change you asked for, and Google Drive shows the same result.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste your Google password, sign-in codes or file contents into the conversation.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Google Drive tool call was rejected locally because its arguments failed the operation schema, request-path safety, destination-folder checks or move rules.

What this means

  • Drive arguments fail the operation schema, provider-path safety, parent selection or move constraints. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Drive arguments fail the operation schema, provider-path safety, parent selection or move constraints.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect exact IDs, parent relationships and required observed preconditions.

How to fix it

  • Check the google_drive call against SCHEMAS in skills/google_drive/models.py: exact file_id/parent_id, timezone-aware ISO timestamps, no owner filter together with drive_id, and an etag or expected_version from a fresh info read for writes. The destination must be an existing, untrashed folder, a move must leave exactly one parent with remove_parent_ids drawn from the current parents, and contents of native Google Docs/Sheets/Slides files cannot be replaced or uploaded as a native type.
  • Use the tool schema, exact IDs, valid timestamps and explicit parent changes. Mutations require an observed version or ETag.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use the tool schema, exact IDs, valid timestamps and explicit parent changes. Mutations require an observed version or ETag.

How to verify the fix

  • Correct structured arguments describe one deliberate supported file operation.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials, content or resumable URLs.
  • Do not blindly repeat uncertain writes.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
